acneiform_rash_grade.label: Current panitumumab skin toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Papules/pustules covering under 10% body-surface area, with or without pruritus or tenderness.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Papules/pustules covering 10-30% body-surface area with or without symptoms and psychosocial/instrumental-ADL impact, or over 30% with mild symptoms.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Papules/pustules covering over 30% body-surface area with moderate/severe symptoms, limiting self-care ADL, or local superinfection requiring oral antibiotics.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences, or extensive superinfection requiring IV antibiotics.

acneiform_rash_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade the dermatological reaction clinically, not acne alone. Record the number of severe episodes and response after withholding. Blistering, skin detachment or infection requires urgent assessment.

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion-related reaction grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade by required interruption, response to symptomatic treatment, recurrence, hospitalisation and life-threatening features.

magnesium_mmol_l.label: Magnesium
magnesium_mmol_l.assessment_guidance: Interpret against the local range and symptoms. Set electrolyte abnormality when correction is needed; this regimen has no source-defined numerical hold threshold.

unexplained_respiratory_symptoms.label: New or worsening unexplained respiratory symptoms

ocular_symptoms.label: New eye pain, redness, light sensitivity or blurred vision

skin_occurrence.label: Number of episodes of grade ≥3 skin toxicity

skin_doses_withheld.label: Doses withheld for this skin episode

skin_failed_recovery.label: Not recovered after the planned 1–2 dose withholding period

severe_skin_complication.label: Severe skin infection, blistering or skin detachment

action.recommendation: Do not administer panitumumab with confirmed interstitial lung disease / pulmonary fibrosis. Discontinue for confirmed treatment-emergent ILD.

rules.explanation: Do not administer panitumumab with confirmed interstitial lung disease / pulmonary fibrosis. Discontinue for confirmed treatment-emergent ILD.

action.recommendation: Withhold and investigate new or worsening respiratory symptoms before further treatment with the implicated medicines.

rules.explanation: Withhold and investigate new or worsening respiratory symptoms before further treatment with the implicated medicines.

action.recommendation: Withhold panitumumab for 1–2 doses; assess severity, recurrence, complications and recovery before any restart.

action.recommendation: Discontinue panitumumab after the fourth grade ≥3 skin-toxicity episode.

rules.explanation: Discontinue panitumumab after the fourth grade ≥3 skin-toxicity episode.

action.recommendation: Discontinue panitumumab if the skin reaction has not recovered after the planned withholding period.

rules.explanation: Discontinue panitumumab if the skin reaction has not recovered after the planned withholding period.

action.recommendation: After recovery below grade 3 following 1–2 withheld doses: panitumumab 100% of original dose. Confirm suitability and previous individual modifications.

action.recommendation: Urgent assessment of severe infected, blistering or peeling skin; withhold panitumumab and consider discontinuation under the SmPC.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue panitumumab for a severe or life-threatening infusion reaction; urgent treatment as appropriate.

action.recommendation: Prompt ophthalmology assessment for possible keratitis; assess risk before continuing panitumumab.

action.recommendation: Correct magnesium, calcium and potassium as indicated. NCCP/SmPC do not specify a numerical panitumumab hold threshold; use clinical severity and local policy.

action.recommendation: NCCP table 1 expects no renal or dialysis adjustment, no mild/moderate hepatic adjustment and no expected severe hepatic adjustment. This does not establish overall treatment suitability.

action.recommendation: Urgent specialist benefit/risk discussion. Avoid breastfeeding during panitumumab and for 2 months after the last dose; pregnancy requires counselling. Do not treat this as routine clearance.

eligibility: Indication as listed in the current official NCCP regimen
Performance status and organ function appropriate for the selected treatment
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
monitoring: FBC, renal and liver profile as specified by the current NCCP regimen
Treatment-specific toxicity monitoring before each administration/cycle
dose_modifications: NCCP table 1 organ function, table 2 skin recurrence/recovery, table 3 infusion/ILD/ocular actions; source-mapped v0.83.5.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP SACT Antiemetic Guidance V6 (2025), table 7, and NCCP 00225 v6 both classify panitumumab as low risk.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for low emetogenic risk
supportive_care.premedication: Not routinely required for panitumumab; local policy after reactions. Chemotherapy antiemetics follow NCCP/local regimen risk.
other_supportive_care: Pre-emptive skin care, sun protection and prescribed therapy under local EGFR policy.
Monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before/during treatment and for up to 8 weeks after; NCCP specifies monthly electrolytes for 2 months post treatment.
Review eye symptoms, lung symptoms, skin infection and diarrhoea; give urgent contact plan.

administration.notes: First dose usually 60 minutes; >1000 mg over 90 minutes. Subsequent doses 30–60 minutes if tolerated. 0.9% NaCl, 0.22 micron filter; incompatible with glucose.
